title: Predictive Disk Failure
exclusions: Reports a device whose `smartctl` JSON says overall SMART health failed, an ATA pre-fail attribute is currently at/below its vendor threshold, or an NVMe critical-warning bit is set. It does not predict the date of failure, treat every nonzero vendor raw attribute as bad, guarantee that a passing drive is healthy, test unread data, diagnose a controller/cable/filesystem, or cover devices hidden behind unsupported RAID controllers. Device discovery, self-test scheduling/results, media-error trends, I/O latency, filesystem integrity, RAID state, backup/restore, and collection health are separate controls. The hourly poll, 70-minute window, severity, retention, and exceptions are local policy. No self-test, repair, wipe, offline action, or replacement is performed and no compliance claim is made.
evidence: After deployment, retain host-to-device/serial/model/controller/workload inventory; supported smartmontools/device/driver versions; least-privilege script and effective input; raw `smartctl -x -j` payloads and exit status; normalized field-map tests for ATA/SCSI/NVMe; device-discovery, poll, staleness, unsupported-device, and parse health; version-controlled `hardware_smart_health_failed` search, ACL, schedule, dispatches, and rows; storage/vendor corroboration and disposition; and dated pass, failed-health, ATA failing-now, NVMe warning-bit, nonzero-raw-only, device-renumber, stale, missing, duplicate, recovery, and routing tests. This documentation-only review executed no SMART command or self-test, indexed no sample, and validated no production disk.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a fixed 70-minute window, ingest the newest normalized sample for `host=server01`, `device_id=wwn-0x5000...`, `smart_status_passed=false`, `ata_failing_now=0`, and `nvme_critical_warning=0`; expect one critical `smart_health_failed` row preserving stable ID, device path, protocol, model, serial, exit status, event/index times, and UC ID. Repeat with `smart_status_passed=true,ata_failing_now=1` and with NVMe critical-warning value 4; expect high `ata_prefail_threshold` and critical `nvme_critical_warning` rows.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for a newest passing sample with zero failing-now attributes and zero NVMe warning bits, even when Reallocated_Sector_Ct or another vendor raw counter is nonzero; for an old failure followed by a newer passing sample; wrong source/type; blank stable device ID; or an event outside the window. Separately prove missing expected device, unsupported bridge, command timeout/permission error, stale sample, malformed JSON, and nonzero smartctl transport/error bits create collection-health findings rather than healthy results.

dataSources: A host-local, read-only scripted poll runs a qualified smartmontools `smartctl -x -j <device>` for every independently discovered governed device and emits `index=hardware sourcetype=hardware:smart` with stable `device_id`/WWN, path, protocol, model, serial, `smart_status_passed`, count of ATA attributes whose normalized `when_failed` is `FAILING_NOW`, numeric `nvme_critical_warning`, smartctl exit status, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Retain protocol-specific raw JSON and discovery/command status; do not normalize raw ATA attribute numbers across vendors as universal failure thresholds.
app: A deployment-owned Splunk app containing device discovery, a least-privilege smartctl JSON scripted input, normalization, expected-device/source-health searches, saved search, fixtures, exact maintenance lookup, dashboard, and runbook. smartmontools is an operating-system package; Splunk Universal Forwarder is a product, not Splunkbase app 617.
spl:
index=hardware sourcetype=hardware:smart earliest=-130m@m latest=-60m@m
| eval endpoint=lower(trim(host)), disk_id=lower(trim(device_id)), smart_passed=lower(trim(tostring(smart_status_passed))), ata_failed=tonumber(ata_failing_now), nvme_warning=tonumber(nvme_critical_warning)
| where len(endpoint)>0 AND len(disk_id)>0
| sort 0 endpoint disk_id -_time -_indextime
| dedup endpoint disk_id
| eval condition=case(smart_passed="false","smart_health_failed",nvme_warning>0,"nvme_critical_warning",ata_failed>0,"ata_prefail_threshold",true(),"normal")
| where condition!="normal"
| eval severity=if(condition IN ("smart_health_failed","nvme_critical_warning"),"critical","high"), event_time=strftime(_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), indexed_time=strftime(_indextime,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), use_case="UC-1.4.4"
| table event_time indexed_time endpoint disk_id device_path protocol model serial_number condition severity smart_passed ata_failed nvme_warning smartctl_exit_status use_case
| sort 0 -severity endpoint disk_id
description: Reports the newest SMART observation for each stable storage-device identity when smartmontools exposes a failed overall health assessment, an ATA pre-fail attribute currently at its vendor threshold, or any NVMe critical-warning bit. It deliberately avoids declaring every nonzero vendor raw counter a failure.
value: A qualified device-health indication can give storage teams time to verify backups, workload redundancy, warranty, and replacement procedure before a drive becomes unusable. Preserving stable identity and protocol-specific evidence improves triage while avoiding false certainty about failure timing or raw attributes whose meaning varies by vendor.
implementation: Inventory every directly visible governed disk by stable WWN/serial, qualify smartmontools JSON and exit semantics for ATA/SCSI/NVMe and supported RAID pass-through, and poll hourly through a least-privilege script. Normalize only documented health signals, monitor discovery/command freshness separately, save the delayed latest-state search, and validate protocol-specific fixtures plus recovery before routing to storage owners.
visualization: Show expected-versus-observed devices and poll health first; then a host/device table with stable ID, path, protocol, model, serial, condition, raw documented indicators, smartctl exit status, sample/index age, workload, backup state, and owner. Add separate protocol-labeled trends for reviewed raw counters; never compare unlike vendor attributes on one universal health scale.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable — no CIM data model for SMART counters.

knownFalsePositives:
A result reflects a documented device signal, but operational interpretation can still be wrong.

1. **Previously failed, now replaced device at the same path** — `/dev/sdX` is not stable identity. Match WWN/serial and lifecycle inventory; retire the old device without deleting its incident.

2. **Unsupported RAID/USB bridge or controller translation** — pass-through can omit, synthesize, or misroute SMART data. Qualify `smartctl -d` behavior and compare controller/vendor tooling; classify unsupported visibility as coverage debt.

3. **Vendor-specific ATA attribute semantics** — a nonzero raw reallocated/pending/error value may be meaningful but is not by itself the standardized threshold crossing used here. Trend it separately under vendor policy; do not add a universal `>0` alert.

4. **Power-cycle or counter reset** — lifetime/power-on and some protocol counters can reset or change representation after firmware/device replacement. Preserve serial, firmware, power-cycle count, and raw JSON.

5. **SMART warning without observed workload impact** — a genuine warning can precede failure by an unknown duration. It is still actionable for verification, but not proof of current outage.

Suppress notification only for an exact stable device identity and condition with owner, change/replacement ticket, start, and finite expiry. Never suppress device discovery, poll/parse/permission, stale-data, unsupported-path, or backup-health findings.

cost.search_load_notes: Hourly low-volume device health samples and a bounded latest-state search; collection cost scales with directly visible disks and smartctl runtime.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and signal boundary

Assign host, storage/controller, backup, workload, Splunk collection/content, and incident owners. Inventory stable WWN/serial, current path, protocol, model/firmware, controller/enclosure/slot, RAID membership, workload, redundancy, backup/restore objective, warranty, and replacement authority for every governed device. Qualify smartmontools against each protocol and controller/pass-through; `smartctl` may require narrowly delegated device access, but the Splunk service must not receive disk-write, wipe, self-test, RAID-change, or filesystem privileges. This documentation review ran no command or product/version matrix and asserts no production validation.

SMART is not a guaranteed failure clock. `smart_status.passed=false` is the device/protocol overall health result exposed by smartctl. ATA attributes have vendor-specific identifiers/raw encodings; use the tool's normalized current threshold result, not `Reallocated_Sector_Ct>0`. NVMe reports a critical-warning bit mask, not ATA attributes. Keep each protocol's evidence intact.

## Step 1 — Discover, collect, and monitor coverage

Use a reviewed wrapper to discover only approved devices, resolve stable identity, and run `smartctl -x -j` with a device-type option qualified for the controller. Parse JSON rather than locale-sensitive tables. Emit one event per device with stable ID, path, protocol, model, serial, smart-status boolean, ATA failing-now count, NVMe critical-warning integer, smartctl exit status, command duration, collector version, `_time`, and raw-reference/hash. Do not expose serials beyond approved roles.

Run hourly only after measuring fleet runtime and controller impact. Splunk scripted-input intervals start after completion, so long commands create drift. Set bounded timeouts and concurrency, and never launch simultaneous tests through a controller. Treat nonzero exit bits individually: transport/command/open/checksum errors are collection quality; health/prefail bits are detection evidence. Retain the complete exit value.

Independent health compares every expected stable device with observations and reports missing/unexpected identity, path remap, unsupported bridge, permission/open/timeout/JSON failure, stale/future time, duplicate route, blank identity, and indexing delay. A missing disk sample is not a passing disk.

## Step 2 — Save and understand the search

Save the sidecar SPL as `hardware_smart_health_failed`. Run hourly over `earliest=-130m@m latest=-60m@m`: a complete 70-minute slice delayed 60 minutes is conservative sample policy, not a vendor threshold. Tune from measured completion/index delay while retaining complete nonoverlapping coverage. The search sorts by event/index time, keeps the newest sample per stable host/device identity, and classifies three documented normalized signals. Overall SMART failure and any NVMe critical-warning bit are critical local routes; current ATA pre-fail threshold is high. Do not add raw vendor attribute comparisons to this generic detector.

## Step 3 — Validate protocols and lifecycle

Replay fixed authentic-shaped ATA, SCSI, and NVMe JSON for every supported smartmontools version. Test boolean/string conversion, warning bits 0 and each supported bit, one/multiple ATA failing-now attributes, nonzero raw values without threshold failure, null/missing fields, nonzero transport exit bits, equal timestamps, duplicate forwarding, late data, path renumbering with stable ID, replacement at same bay, old failure followed by pass, and exact time boundaries. Assert source health independently.

In a disposable lab, compare indexed output to the same `smartctl -x -j` payload and the controller/vendor management UI or CLI. Use vendor-provided test media or historical approved failure payloads; do not damage a disk or force failure solely to test. Verify a passing result does not erase prior evidence and a removed device becomes an inventory-health finding. Keep draft until owners approve protocol mappings, fixtures, coverage, timing, routing, dashboard, and response.

## Step 4 — Operationalize without unsafe automation

Alert wording states the exact signal, device identity, sample age, protocol, model/serial, controller/slot, workload, RAID/redundancy, backup/restore status, warranty, and owner. Responders verify raw JSON and current vendor/controller state; confirm identity and physical slot; review SMART self-test/error logs where safe; inspect kernel/controller/RAID/path and workload I/O evidence; validate backups and redundancy; then follow vendor replacement procedure. Never run a self-test on latency-sensitive production, offline a disk, fail a member, rebuild an array, unmount a filesystem, stop a workload, or reboot automatically from this result.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot and close

- **No device data:** check expected inventory, discovery filters, path permissions, controller pass-through, smartctl type option, timeout, script exit/runtime, input stanza, forwarding, index, and RBAC.
- **Raw counters trigger concern but no row:** this generic rule intentionally uses documented health/threshold signals. Apply a model/vendor-approved trend in separate content with evidence and boundaries.
- **NVMe warning unclear:** decode the retained bit mask against the deployed specification/tool output and inspect NVMe health/error logs; do not label all bits media failure.
- **Path changed:** reconcile WWN/serial and enclosure slot. Never close by matching `/dev/sdX` alone.
- **SMART passes while I/O fails:** SMART cannot cover every failure. Investigate kernel, controller, path, RAID, latency, filesystem, and workload evidence.

Close only after stable identity is confirmed, source health is current, vendor/controller and workload evidence is assessed, backup/redundancy risk is addressed, repair/replacement or accepted risk is documented, and an owner-approved observation interval has no unexplained recurrence.
grandmaExplanation: We read each drive's own health report and call out the warning states the drive actually declares. We do not pretend that every changing counter predicts exactly when a disk will fail.
hardware: ATA/SATA/SAS/SCSI/NVMe devices visible to supported smartmontools through the host or a qualified controller pass-through. Stable WWN/serial, controller path, enclosure/slot, workload, RAID membership, warranty, and replacement history are required; a Linux device path alone is not identity.
